 COVID-19
 What is coronavirus?
 Coronaviruses are a large family of viruses that
 are known to cause illness ranging from the
 common cold to more severe diseases such as
 Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) and
 Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS)
 Common among animals- zoonotic, animal to
 human transmission
 Is a respiratory disease caused by SARS-C0V -2
 Virus
 COVID-19
 First reported in Wuhan city, Hubei Province,
 China in December,2019
 Started from local seafood market, known to sell
 live and freshly slaughtered hunted animals
 BAT
 SNAKES, PANGOLINS( an ant-eater)

 How COVID-19 Spreads
 The virus is thought to spread mainly from person-to-person.
 Between people who are in close contact with one another (within
 about 6 feet) for 15 minutes or more
 Through respiratory droplets produced when an infected person
 coughs, sneezes or talks.
 These droplets can land in the mouths or noses of people who are
 nearby or possibly be inhaled into the lungs.
 Some recent studies have suggested that COVID-19 may be spread by
 people who are not showing symptoms.
 (The best way to prevent illness is to avoid being exposed to
 this virus.)
 COVID-19 (coronavirus) in children
 Children of all ages can become ill with coronavirus disease
 2019 (COVID-19) and can transmit it to others.
 Children don't become sick as often as adults.
 Most children have mild symptoms or no symptoms.
 Most children recover within one to two weeks, adults 2-6
 weeks
 In the US, hospitalization rates for children are also much
 lower than for adults-10% of all COVID-19 cases.
 COVID-19 (coronavirus) in children
 Children with underlying conditions, such as obesity,
 diabetes and asthma, congenital heart disease, genetic
 conditions like sickle cell disease or conditions affecting the
 nervous system or metabolism are also at higher risk of
 serious illness with COVID-19
 Symptoms of COVID-19
 Fever or chills
 Cough
 Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
 Fatigue
 Muscle or body aches, Diarrhea, Nausea or vomiting
 Headache
 New loss of taste or smell
 Sore throat
 Congestion or runny nose
 COVID 19 Advanced Symptoms
 Individuals should seek immediate medical attention
 if they display the following advanced symptoms:
 Trouble breathing
 Persistent pain or pressure in the chest
 New confusion
 Inability to wake or stay awake
 Bluish lips or face
 Prevention of COVID 19
 Regularly and thoroughly clean your hands with soap and running
 water for at least 20 seconds
 If soap and water are not readily available, use a hand sanitizer
 ‘hand rub’ that contains at least 60% alcohol.
 Maintain at least 1 meter physical distance
 Avoid going to crowded places
 Avoid touching your Face ( eyes, nose and mouth).
 Practice good respiratory hygiene (covering your mouth and nose
 with your bent elbow or tissue when you cough or sneeze).
 Stay home and self-isolate even with minor symptoms such as
 cough, headache, mild fever, until you recover.
 Prevention of COVID 19
 Avoid close contact with anyone who has cold or flu-like
 symptoms. If possible, maintain 6 feet between the person who is
 sick and other household members.
 Clean and disinfect regularly touched surfaces frequently.
 This includes toys, play areas, tables, doorknobs, light
 switches, countertops, rails, handles, desks, phones,
 keyboards, toilets, faucets, and sinks.
 Always wear a face mask while in public spaces including
 schools
 Avoid shaking hands or hugging people.
 Avoid social gatherings eg parties

 Wearing of Face Masks
 Masks help prevent spread of the virus from one person to
 another.
 Types of Masks
 Surgical masks
 N95 masks
 Cloth masks
 MOE Response
 Government announced the closure of all
 schools and learning institutions on March
 15, 2020, as part of the measures to control
 the spread of COVID-19
 Ministry developed Kenya Basic Education
 COVID-19 Emergency Response Plan ,
 2020
 Inauguration of Education COVID 19
 response committee on 12th May 2020
 Which recommended:
 • Gradual safe reopening of learning institutions
 • Staggered and in shifts where applicable
 Priority be accorded to finalist and examination
 classes
 Grade 4, CBC pioneer
 Reopening process( prior to reopening, part of
 reopening, with schools reopened
 Government implementing phased reopening
 which commenced from 12th October, 2020
 Guidelines on Health & Safety Protocols
 Guidelines provide prevention, early detection,
 infection control and management measures of
 COVID-19 in educational institutions.
 To be understood by teachers, non-teaching staff,
 learners, parents and entire school community
 Enable institution leadership, management and
 communities to prepare for safe reopening of schools
 Basic infrastructure to be put in place to facilitate the
 recommended infection control measures and adhere to
 physical/ social distancing measures.
 Reopening Focus
 Pro-poor interventions
 School Response
 School COVID 19 Response team-focal persons
 Temperature screening - entrance to the compound
 Hand washing facilities (soap and running water)-
 multiple places
 Hand sanitizing facilities- multiple places
 Maintain at least 1 meter physical distance between
 learners at all times ( classes, dining, labs, dormitories
 etc)
 Wearing of face masks by all learners, teachers and other
 staff.
 School Response
 Cleaning and Disinfection of the classrooms at the end of the day
 Fumigation
 Avoid going to crowded places
 Avoid touching your Face ( eyes, nose and mouth).
 EIC materials displayed in strategic places
 School transport- social distance, sanitizing, disinfection
 Reduce number of visitors in schools
 Well ventilated
 Pedal-operated waste collection bins with liners at point
 of use/Dust bin , non-touch
 School Response
 Holding room for those who may have fever or any other
 symptoms suggestive of COVID 19
 Emergence contact
 Linkages to a health facility
 Ambulance services
 PPE for emergency response
 Psychosocial and mental health wellness
 Stay home and self-isolate even with minor symptoms
 such as cough, headache, mild fever, until you recover.
 Stay Healthy
 Social assessment –Who is at a higher risk?
 Younger children (e.g., preschool)
 Anyone who has trouble breathing
 Anyone who is unconscious, incapacitated
 People who are deaf or hard of hearing- not read lips
 People with intellectual and developmental disabilities, mental
 health conditions or other sensory sensitivities
 Vulnerable and marginalized groups
 Persons / learners with underlying conditions, such as obesity,
 diabetes and asthma, congenital heart disease, genetic conditions
 like sickle cell disease or conditions affecting the nervous system
 or metabolism
